articleTitle: The Influence of Permanent Magnet Length and Magnet Type on Flux-control of Axial Flux Hybrid Excited Electrical Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This paper presents the influence of permanent magnet (PM) parameters and axial length of PMs on a DC field control range of a hybrid excited axial-flux (HEAF) machine design. Based on 3-D finite-element analysis (3D-FEA), a flux-control range (FCR), flux density distribution, and no-load phase back-EMF waveforms have been performed. Moreover, FEA predictions of back-EMF under different DC field currents have been compared with experimental results obtained from a prototype HEAF machine with NdFeB magnets on the rotor.

articleTitle: Automated Test Stand for Transformer Inrush Current Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Paper discusses the design idea, construction of the prototype measurement unit and experimental verification of an automated test stand for transformer inrush current identification. Transformers of different size and construction are key components in power systems and power supply units. Proposed test stand construction allows automated inrush current measurement and maximum inrush current identification for tested transformers. Presented experimental results are provided for toroidal core transformers.

articleTitle: Simulink Modeling of Multiphase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The subject of the article is a computer model of a multi-phase squirrel cage induction motor with a stator number phases greater than 3. This model is written in the Matlab / Simulink language and is presented graphically in the form of a multi-terminal block. A system of differential equations describing a multiphase motor was introduced by the use of Simulink library blocks. This system of equations takes into account the interaction of higher spatial harmonics. The block of equations is connected to the external power circuit by means of the so-called ideal transformers. This allows for modeling not only the electric drive, but also the internal waveforms of the converter and the power supply system. Application of the model was illustrated by the operation of a nine-phase motor powered by a frequency-controlled voltage source inverter at a variable supply sequence and referred to measurements.

articleTitle: Problematic Applications of Fractional Derivatives in Electrotechnics and Electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: A critical review of selected fractional derivative approaches applied to the electromagnetic field theory and electrical circuits theory is presented in the paper. Particular attention has been paid to frequent formal errors and to reservations related to unclear physical meaning of the applied parameters, as well as to the formulas found inconsistent with the basic laws of electrodynamics.

articleTitle: Research on Surge Voltage Withstand of Medium Voltage Vacuum Reed Relay
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This paper presents results of experiments carried out in order to determine surge voltage withstand of vacuum reed relay which is not given in the catalogue notes. Three MV vacuum switches were tested with standardized 1.2/50 μs voltage surge. Breakdown voltages of each analyzed reed relay were determined. The same devices (after breakdown) were tested once more in order to examine the insulation properties. As it was observed, after two electrical breakdowns, electric withstand of each reed relay decreased significantly. Based on conducted measurements it was determined that the breakdown voltage is twice as high as 60 s DC withstand voltage provided by the manufacturer. The paper also presents the analysis of electric arc erosion of electric contacts after the electrical breakdown. An optical microscope was used to perform observations of damaged surfaces. Additionally, roughness profiles of damaged contact surface were measured.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Sampling Method For Power Measurement On A Compact PLC Controller - Error Elimination Due To Serial Sampling
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The high demands made on power supply systems, and consequently on electric devices used in industrial processes, cause the need to ensure the appropriate quality of power supply. The basic parameters of the power systems are: the rms-values of the current, voltage and active and reactive power consumed by the electric loads. In previous papers the authors have studied the use of a low-frequency sampling method for measuring these basic power system parameters showing that this method can be easily applied in simple microcontrollers and PLC controllers. This article discusses the influence of the technical limitations of measurement devices on the measured rms-values of the current and voltage as well as on reactive and active power values. The result of this study is the proposal of error reduction of the low-frequency measurement method while using it on simple microcontrollers and compact PLC controllers. Laboratory tests carried out using an Mitsubishi FX5 compact PLC controller confirmed the correctness of the proposed method of reducing the measurement error.

Author Keywords: low-frequency sampling method for measurement of current and voltage and power
power measurement using compact PLC controllers

articleTitle: Reduction of switching losses in three-phase three-level voltage source inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors are ones of basic switching elements in voltage source inverters with medium and high power rating. The switching losses in these transistors can be significantly reduced using different methods which allow to switch transistors at their voltage or current that are close to zero. In many soft switching systems auxiliary circuits consist of capacitors connected in parallel to the main transistors and resonant inductors which are connected in series to auxiliary transistors. These connections are not recommended because the main or auxiliary transistor may be damaged during disturbances in control systems. Due to these drawbacks, the patented solution, wherein the above disadvantages do not occur, is presented in this paper. Special attention was paid to total losses in the presented soft switching system; these losses were compared with the switching losses in an inverter operating without any soft switching system. This comparison was made for an inverter with a rated power of about 1.2 MW.

articleTitle: Predictive SVM Control Method of AC/DC Converter with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This paper presents simulation results of infinite control set model predictive control implemented into three-phase AC/DC converter. The connection between the converter and electric grid is made through LCL filter which is characterized by a better reduction of grid current distortions and smaller (cheaper) components in comparison to L-type filter. On the other hand, this type of filter can cause strong resonance at specific current harmonic which are efficiently suppressed by the control strategy which focuses on the strict control of the voltage vector of input filter capacitors. The presented method links benefits of using linear control methods based on space vector modulator and the non-linear ones which allow obtaining good control performance in steady state as well as in a transient state.

articleTitle: Changes in the Spectral Power Distribution of Light Sources for Smart Lighting
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Sunlight depending on the time of the day, is characterized by different spectral nature. The human body uses it to regulate its daily activity. To adjust the level of illumination and spectrum to the natural cycle of daily activity of the body we use lighting installations using smart light sources. The article presents the results of measurements of spectral characteristics, luminous flux and color temperature of incandescent, fluorescent and electroluminescence sources used in smart lighting installations.

articleTitle: Field Calculations of an Induction Cage Motor Taking into Account Magnetic Core Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Magnetic core anisotropy of induction motors can disturb control processes or diagnostic procedures. This paper presents the level of secondary mechanical and electrical effects generated by an anisotropic magnetic core of two-pole cage motor. 2D field calculations were used to determine the magnetic field co-energy and the fluxes linked with three phase winding supplied with three phase current sources. The model used for calculating the main field had the rotor without any cage bars. The reduced field model for calculating the stator leakage field included the stator core and the rotor core teeth only. Waveforms of the magnetic field co-energy allowed to determine the harmonics components of the electromagnetic torque. The waveforms of the phase fluxes were the basis for determining the spectra of the phase voltages symmetrical components in an idle run and in a start-up state. The frequency levels components due to the rotor core anisotropy are shown. According to the reciprocity theorem the analogous spectra should be predicted in the currents when motor is supplied with the voltage sources.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of PM Disc Generator with Iron Cores of Stator Coils
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents a model of disc generator with permanent magnets and with iron cores inside the stator coils. The article focuses on the circuit model of the permanent magnet generator of axial magnetization with a stator which contains the nonoverlapping coils with modified magnetic circuit design. The aim of this work was to determine the flux-density distribution in three-phase generator magnetic circuit. Basing on this distribution, the circuit model parameters such as inductances, fluxes linked with the windings and qualitative characteristics of the cogging torque were determined for axial flux machine. To confirm the usefulness of the proposed models, the parameters of mathematical model obtained from analytical considerations were verified basing on 3D field analyses for the exemplary generator design.

articleTitle: Novel Concept of PM Electric Machine with Magnetic Barriers and Excitation Coils in the Rotor
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents a hybrid excited electric machine with permanent embedded magnets and excitation windings in the rotor structure to electric vehicle drivers. Finite element analysis (FEA) of the proposed machine design has been used to analyse a field-control capability under different field currents. According to simulating research a prototype machine has been designed, built and tested. Experimental results of back-emf and the cogging torque waveforms achieved at different DC field excitation current have been compared with FEA results.

articleTitle: Influence of Rotor Design on Field Regulation Capability of Hybrid Excited Electric Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper contains results of simulation research of a hybrid excited machine - Electrically Controlled Permanent Magnet Excited Synchronous Machine (ECPMSM) - with three construction concepts of the rotor. Selected experimental results of the prototype with two rotor's construction variants are also presented. In addition, in order to compare the properties at high rotational speeds for presented rotor designs, the expected performance, i.e. the range of speed and torque of the machine and the possibility of the excitation field weakening, were evaluated.

articleTitle: A Possibility of the State of Charge Monitoring of the Lead-Acid Battery by Means of Current Pulses of a Given Value
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents the results of testing the internal resistance changes of the lead-acid battery as a function of accumulated charge. In order to measure the internal resistance, a short current pulses of a given value at specified time intervals were forced in the battery. The internal series resistance of the battery equivalent circuit was determined as the quotient of the measured voltage jump to the value of the current pulse. The measurements were carried out in time windows of a given length. The experiment showed that the internal resistance during discharging is monotonically variable in relation to the remaining charge in the battery and this method can be used to estimation the state of charge of the battery. In contrast, during loading, no such dependence is observed.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of a Rotor Axis Stability with a Passive Magnetic Bearing System
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents the results of modelling the characteristics of passive magnetic bearings. Bearings composed of one or three ring magnet systems were considered. The forces of centring the magnets against each other and axial force repelling magnets are analysed. The simulations performed the function of the mutual position of the magnet rings, taking into account the change of the displacement parameter in the direction of the z and r axes and the angle of displacement between the planes of the rings.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of Currents Flowing in High Voltage Power Substations During Ground Short - Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This article presents a method for determining the distribution of ground short-circuits in high voltage substations, in particular determining the value of currents flowing into substations grounding. Knowledge of these currents is important to assess the risk of electric shock hazard within the substation area. The EMTP-ATP program was used in the research, in which the structure of the analyzed systems was created. The results of calculations made for a selected high voltage substation in various work configurations are presented.

articleTitle: Resonant, High Voltage Power Supply for Non-Thermal Plasma Reactors
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper describes a novel topology of a high-voltage pulse generator for non-thermal plasma supply. Proposed converter prototype generates high voltage pulses up to 35 kV. Presented article includes the presentation of a new, resonant converter topology with analytical and simulation based description of operation principles and a discussion of most important generator features. Presented topology is well suited for supplying both the Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD) and the pulsed corona discharge (PCD) plasma reactors. Its construction is insensitive to short-circuits in the load.

articleTitle: Computer Analysis of the Steady States of a 21 MVA Superconducting Transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This article describes the computational model of a single phase 21 MV superconducting transformer. The project required the use of appropriate mathematical models for all nonlinear elements. For the construction of the magnetic circuit, the core was made of PN ET114-27 sheet. The mathematical Jiles-Atherton description of the second level was used to determine the non-linear magnetic circuit of the transformer. This model made it possible to reconstruct the magnetic hysteresis loop for the adopted sheet. Using the developed model of the superconducting and conventional transformer with the power of 21 MVA, hysteresis loops were generated and the obtained values of idle current, idle losses, short-circuit voltage and losses in the windings were compared.

articleTitle: Correlation Between Wind and Solar Renewable Energy Generation and Electricity Consumption in Poland, Derived to Estimate the Energy Storage Needs
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Correlation coefficient between renewable energy generation based on wind or solar and electricity consumption across the entire Polish Power System, industrial customers and typical household in Poland, enables estimating the volume of electricity, which can be directly transferred to customers, to supply energy consumption needs and the volume of electricity, which should be stored to secure continuous supply. This volume gives indication of the energy storage capacity required for different type of customers.

articleTitle: The Use of Modern Methods of Modelling Power Converters in the Design Process
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: In the article the possibility of using modern methods of computer modelling in the design process of power electronic converters with control circuits was presented. As part of research a representative power electronic converter with an additional system enabling registration of selected parameters was tested. Next, identification of the laboratory model and verification of the estimated dynamic models was carried out, using the System Identification Toolbox from Matlab. These models can be used for simple and fast optimization of the PI controllers, which is very important in the designing of power electronics systems. The research shows a significant impact of switching frequency on identification process accuracy with delays of digital controller taken into account.

articleTitle: Power Losses in the Low Voltage Switchboard
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents the results of research, which indicate what simplifications in mathematical models can be used during the analysis of the temperature distribution in low-voltage switchgear. Elements that significantly influence the final test results are indicated, and those whose modeling method doesn't affect the accuracy of the final results.

articleTitle: Frequency and Parametric Characteristics of Direct Current Pulse Conversion Filter of a Contactless Electric Locomotive
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Dependences of the level of receiving circuit current pulsation of a contactless electric locomotive while using direct current pulse-width converter in the circuit to control traction drive upon the parameters of π-shaped filter components and commutation frequency of a converter have been obtained basing upon the use of topological method of directed graphs. The proposed method has made it possible to calculate filter parameters and give certain recommendations as for the converter commutation frequency according to the condition of providing minimum level of current pulsation of the electric locomotive receiving circuit.

articleTitle: The Influence of Power Lines Non-Homogeneity on PLC Data Transmission Protocols Efficacy
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: In the paper the results of simulation and laboratory experiments relating the influence of features and characteristics of low voltage energetic cables existing in Polish grid infrastructure on efficacy of measurement data transmission via power cables. From data transfer perspective any piece of power cable is a transmission line with certain parameters. The impact of that parameters with a special emphasis on heterogeneity of cable paths on possible transmission quality degradation has been studied in the paper.

articleTitle: The Influence of Permanent Magnet Amount on No-load Parameters of Hybrid Excited Claw Pole Machine with Laminated Rotor
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents chosen research results of Hybrid Excited Claw Pole Machine with Laminated Rotor (HECPMLR). In introduction types and variants of hybrid excited electric machines have been briefly presented. Then a detailed proposal for the new construction of the claw pole machine was presented. During the research the influence of the permanent magnets width and current in the excitation coil on the back-emf and cogging torque in the claw pole machine with hybrid excitation and laminated rotor structure have been analyzed.

articleTitle: Receiver Originated Noise Immunity of PLC OSGP Protocol
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Data transmission efficacy depends on interference noise within the transmission band. This apply in particular for smart electric meters using powerline as the transmission medium. The results of laboratory tests of receiver originated noise for the most popular in Poland PLC-OSGP protocol are reported in the paper. Experimentally measured frequency responses for the home appliances potentially influencing the PLC transmission quality are also presented.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Measurements Based on its Geometrical Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper shows that a generalized unique definition of additive reactive power derives from the general definition of active power. Unlike active power, reactive power must be independent of the conversion of electric energy into work and heat. This independence is achieved if one of the waveforms - the current in the scalar voltage and current product (specifying active power) - is replaced by a special orthogonal waveform (a current derivative). Some properties of reactive power defined in this way are presented. Based on the theory proposed by Illiovici, a measurement stand was designed and built to allow measurement verification of theory and simulation tests.

articleTitle: Improving Robustness of the MRAS-based Speed Estimator to Variability of Induction Motor Electromagnetic Parameters Resulting from the Rotor Deep Bar Effect
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents selected study results for assessing robustness of the considered configurations of the Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) based speed estimator to variability of induction motor electromagnetic parameters resulted from the rotor deep bar effect. As pointed out in the literature, the current model of the rotor flux space vector, which has been used as the adjustable model of the classical MRAS-based speed estimator, shows sensitivity to rotor electromagnetic parameter variability. The combination of the adequately transformed voltage model and the current model of the rotor flux space vector leads to the estimation system of this vector which is characterized by less sensitivity to the rotor electromagnetic parameter variability, when compared with the current model, in a wide range of slip frequency changes. The employment of the resulted voltage-current model of the rotor flux space vector as the adjustable model of the MRAS-based speed estimator has allowed for considerable increase in its robustness to the variability of IM rotor electromagnetic parameters arisen from the rotor deep bar effect. The presented verification investigations of the analyzed MRAS-based speed estimators have been carried out on the basis of induction motor physical quantities registered experimentally on the laboratory test bench.

articleTitle: Parameters of the Hysteresis Model of Transformer Steel Sheets
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Lines of the field strength and flux density in corners and in points, where columns and jokes are connected, are usually not parallel to the rolling direction. The hysteresis loop obtained for directions other than the rolling direction differs greatly in comparison to the hysteresis loop which are measured along the rolling direction. The paper describes briefly modification of the “classic” model of the magnetic hysteresis. Special attention has been paid to principles of determination of the modified model parameters and their dependences on the direction of the magnetization process in transformer sheets. Numerical calculations were performed for chosen transformer sheet and for several values of the field strength. Calculated loops were compared to the measured hysteresis loops.

articleTitle: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control of Current Source Inverter for Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Three-phase current source rectifier is a very good solution for connecting photovoltaic modules to the grid because of its boosting nature. However, an LC filter included on the grid side enhances grid current distortions. Proper control can reduce the impact of those disadvantages. The paper presents a new FCS-MPC method for the CSI combined with MPPT algorithm. The algorithm provides unity power factor and low grid current distortions, proven in simulation results.

articleTitle: Impact of Rotor Design on Motion Properties of a Synchronized Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents the results of tests of low-power induction motors operating at synchronous rotation speed. This working condition was achieved by introducing changes to the rotor shape design. The changes caused unevenness in the air gap between the stator and the rotor. The reluctance torque created in this structure enables a synchronous operation. The paper presents the results of experiments of a series of numerical simulations carried out for structures with various shapes of large teeth on squirrel-cage rotors. All considered structures maintained the continuity of the rotor cage.

articleTitle: The Investigation of The Properties of High-voltage Transformer in Nonthermal Plasma Pulse Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2018 14th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This paper describes the investigation of the high-voltage pulse transformer, which is a special one due to the fact that the switching-mode power supply, in which it works, operates in a push-pull topology. This topology is not typical and used unusually for high input voltages, however, for plasma applications, it can have positives. This paper not only shows and includes the description of the topology of the supply, but it also reveals the chosen details of the project and the construction of the high -voltage transformer. A special attention has been given to the observation an output current and voltage waveforms. Attention has been given to the evaluation of short pulses - effectiveness to entail plasma reactor's ignition.
